newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP backs changes to calves directive.
newsitem.headline: EP backs changes to calves directive.

text.p: The European Parliament's committee on agriculture has adopted a report calling for changes to a proposed directive protecting calves on farms.
The report by rapporteur Raul Miguel Rosado Fernandes concludes that the minimum sizes of calf pens should be specified in centimetres to aid monitoring.
It also backs derogations for smaller herds from the provision that all calves over eight weeks old should be housed in groups by introducing a minimum herd size of ten animals.
It criticises the Commission for planning to postpone a ban on individual pens until January 1, 2008 and says the date to be brought forward to the year 2003 "with the aim of boosting credibility".

It wants discussion on the feeding and the dimensions of calf pens and adds that the colour and taste of veal should not mean that calves are fed a nutritionally unbalanced diet which inhibits their natural development.
